c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_closure_gc.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: Escaped eval closures must capture the actual native Environment, which the inherited C helper does not pass.

c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_lexical_bindings.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: The inherited C DirectEval helper does not receive the caller lexical environment.

c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_lexical_errors.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: The inherited C direct-eval path lacks lexical binding and TDZ metadata.

c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_nested.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: The static C DirectEval entry lacks the native caller Environment; nested dynamic calls use the shared interpreter metadata path.

c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_nested_global.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: The LLVM direct-eval extension retains the original global or function context through nested dynamic calls.

c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_private_context_boundary.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: The inherited C direct-eval path also lacks enclosing class lexical metadata.

c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_sloppy_boundary.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: The inherited C helper silently evaluates globally instead of injecting caller bindings.

c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_super_context_boundary.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: The inherited C direct-eval path also lacks the method home object.

c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_source_context.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: Source-site lexical and new.target context is recorded only by the LLVM direct-eval extension.

c_oracle_limitations.name: eval_this_arguments.js
c_oracle_limitations.reason: The inherited C direct-eval helper substitutes global this and has no caller argument environment.

qualification: Linux x86-64 host native/lli targeted tests. Runtime/bridge ASan enabled; leak checking disabled for sandbox restriction. Generated LLVM bodies are not fully ASan instrumented. Dynamic source compiles to Hermes bytecode. Explicit direct-eval boundaries are separate rejection contracts, not successful Node semantic comparisons. Shared frontend and runtime corrections affect both C and LLVM paths. No full ECMAScript/Test262 result, physical hardware result or speedup is claimed.
